after.text:
A.2 Arithmetic L-functions
      Loosely speaking, arithmetic L-functions are those Dirichlet series with appropriate
functional equations and Euler products which should satisfy a Riemann Hypothesis. Sel-
berg has given specific requirements11 which seem likely to make this definition precise.
Arithmetic L-functions arise in many situations: from the representation theory of groups
associated with number fields, from automorphic forms on arithmetic groups acting on sym-
metric spaces, and from the harmonic analysis on these spaces.

ensemble. For more details on the statistics of the zeros of the zeta function and other
L-functions, see L-functions and Random Matrix Theory3.

related_synthesis_entries.claim: Logarithmic derivatives, Tauberian arguments, summatory cancellation, and explicit formulas provide multiple interfaces translating zero location into arithmetic error or positivity statements.
related_synthesis_entries.limit: The criteria have different hypotheses and levels of quantitative strength; this synthesis does not make them interchangeable proofs.
related_synthesis_entries.title: Prime-zero translation pipeline

related_synthesis_entries.claim: A wide family of RH equivalences replaces direct zero location by positivity, density, approximation error, or determinant tests over increasingly rich witnesses.
related_synthesis_entries.limit: Equivalence alone does not identify a tractable witness or algorithm, and several displayed formulas need scan verification.
